Stable bandwidth expansion for FTR measurement in modal-frequency-mismatched MEMS gyroscopes over a wide temperature range
Intelligent identification of bearing dynamic parameters using a two-stage physics-informed residual KAN with TSA and frequency-domain integration
Finite-time backstepping control for nonlinear active suspension with time-delay compensation via IT2 fuzzy observer
Predicting chaotic average output power in bi-stable energy harvesters through unstable periodic orbits: Theoretical analysis and experimental validation
Utility-driven adaptive model selection for digital twinning
abstract: Digital twins have become central to modern engineering by providing interconnected virtual representations that mirror the behavior of physical assets. Their effectiveness, however, depends critically on the fidelity and efficiency of the underlying computational models used for decision support. This work introduces an adaptive Bayesian framework for quantifying and optimizing the fidelity, efficiency, and overall utility of such virtual representations when approximating system responses in decision-oriented contexts. By integrating reduced-order models (ROMs) within a Bayesian inference and decision-theoretic setting, the framework identifies, at any point in time, the lowest-cost model capable of delivering the required predictive accuracy across all quantities of interest, while rigorously accounting for the uncertainty associated with each model resolution. The approach maximizes an expected-utility function that balances two competing attributes: (i) precision, reflecting the effect of over- or under-estimating target quantities on decision quality, and (ii) computational efficiency, ensuring feasibility for real-time inference. Leveraging continuously assimilated monitoring data, the framework performs this model selection recursively, enabling the virtual twin to evolve in tandem with the physical system. The resulting methodology supports automated decisions on whether to retain the current model, switch to an alternative resolution, or trigger retraining—thus establishing a pathway toward adaptive, trustworthy digital twins for engineering decision support.

title: Kalman filter-aided vision transformer for seismic deformation measurement of self-centering structures
A unified framework for equation discovery and dynamic prediction of hysteretic systems
abstract: Hysteresis is a nonlinear phenomenon with memory effects, where a system's output depends on both its current state and past states. It is prevalent in various physical and mechanical systems, such as yielding structures under seismic excitation, ferromagnetic materials, and piezoelectric actuators. Analytical models like the Bouc-Wen model are often employed but rely on idealized assumptions and careful parameter calibration, limiting their applicability to diverse or mechanism-unknown behaviors. Existing equation discovery approaches for hysteresis are often system-specific or rely on predefined model libraries, which limit their flexibility and ability to capture the hidden mechanisms. To address these challenges, this research classifies equation discovery problems for hysteretic systems and develops a unified framework in which the state-space form is reformulated, and hysteretic variables are treated as trainable parameters from data. The framework further employs symbolic regression (SR) to automatically recover explicit governing equations without relying on predefined libraries, unlike methods such as sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is effective in recovering governing equations for hysteretic systems, even in a challenging Full Equation Discovery setting, where prior information is extremely limited, and solving the equations naturally enables the dynamic prediction of hysteretic systems.

title: An acoustic velocity-constrained equivalent source method for acoustic imaging with the acoustic vector sensor array
Hydraulic system compound fault diagnosis based on decoupling-oriented feature optimization and uncertainty-aware evidential fusion
Nonlinear structural health monitoring of a planar Slider-Crank linkage using VAM and HHG techniques
Revisiting the characteristics of repetitive transients caused by rotating machinery faults and A new fault signature indicator for quantification and extraction
Fault transient extraction for rolling bearing fault diagnosis based on coefficient-orthogonal nonnegative matrix factorization
The adaptive blind filtering: A unified framework for repetitive transient extraction linking blind deconvolution and narrowband envelope analysis
Convolution-based reformulation and Kalman-filter identification of short-time kernel operators for seat-human vibration modeling
abstract: Accurate modeling of seat-human vibration dynamics is important for response prediction and vibration-control design. However, practical seat-human systems may exhibit locally varying dynamic behavior because of occupant-seat interactions, contact-condition changes, and operating-condition variability, which limits the effectiveness of models based on globally fixed mass, damping, and stiffness parameters. This study proposes a short-time dynamic-operator identification framework based on a convolution-based reformulation of the classical vibration model and Kalman-filter-based recursive estimation. The local input-output relationship between the relative motion and head acceleration is represented by three low-order equivalent operators derived from the temporal moments of an equivalent convolution relationship. Within each short-time window, the operators are treated as a slowly varying state vector and are recursively identified using measured relative displacement, velocity, and acceleration. The operators obtained from multiple windows are subsequently aligned and averaged to construct a reusable finite-support operator representation for prediction on unseen data segments without further parameter updating. The framework was evaluated using vertical floor and head acceleration measurements obtained from three different truck-seat systems under idle-in-park conditions. Multiple operator lengths and identification-prediction data partitions were examined. The results show that the proposed method consistently reconstructs the dominant waveform, local response variation, and phase evolution of the measured head acceleration using limited identification data. Baseline comparisons further indicate that the time-varying operator model provides more accurate response reconstruction than fixed operator, fixed-parameter mass-damping-stiffness (MCK), and time-varying MCK models. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for short-time identification and extended prediction of seat-human vibration responses under the tested operating conditions. Further validation is required before extending the method to other excitation conditions or dynamic systems.

title: A lightweight multi-scale ensemble learning framework for seismic fragility assessment of damped outrigger structures
Beyond the fit: assessing bias-variance trade-off in johnson-cook constitutive modeling for AA5182
abstract: Physics-based predictive models often contain known inadequacies due to their simplified representation of underlying physical systems, introducing systematic deviations from reality. Despite this, they tend to generalize better than their purely empirical counterparts and are often the only tools available to evaluate or predict the performance of complex engineering systems. In this paper, we present a principled framework for calibrating simulation models with known deficiencies against experimental data and for evaluating their predictive ability. Discussions explore the modeling of a cylindrical AA5182 aluminum alloy specimen tested in compression at temperatures ranging from 200 - 500°C, and at strain rates of 0.001 and 1s-1. A finite element model of the specimen is constructed in Abaqus/CAE 2025 using the Johnson-Cook constitutive model, a common choice for simulating alloy behavior due to its computational efficiency. The Johnson-Cook model has several alloy-specific parameters that must be calibrated against experimental data, introducing uncertainty into the finite element model predictions. Additionally, its simplified treatment of strain hardening leads to systematic discrepancies between simulated and observed material responses, which can be inferred through an independent, empirically trained error function. Herein, we explicitly account for these uncertainties and discrepancies and evaluate the bias-variance trade-off in the model predictions. We propose a metric, Calibration Flexibility Measure, to quantitatively evaluate the trade-off between goodness-of-fit and model complexity. Key decisions, such as selection of calibration parameters, integration of prior knowledge, and definition of model-form error are explored to assess and characterize their effects on posterior distributions and predictive performance.

A physics-based analytical model of blade tip sensor waveforms for vibration parameter identification
Adaptive short time fractional Fourier transform and its applications in locomotive gear fault diagnosis

A dual-arch compliant mechanism based piezoelectric inertial actuator with configurable driving foot trajectory for cross-scale stepping and scanning
abstract: This study proposed a novel multi-mode piezoelectric inertial actuator with a symmetric dual-arch compliant mechanism where the driving foot trajectory can be modulated by adjusting a single configurable voltage coefficient. In particular, the proposed actuator can achieve three different cross-scale motion modes: 1) high speed stepping mode, 2) smooth tracking mode, as well as 3) surge stepping mode with ultra-fine stepping resolution, which significantly extends the motion capabilities of existing inertial actuators with only a stepping mode. The proposed design was theoretically modeled and analyzed, where the key parameters were optimized. To achieve cross-scale stepping and scanning, a dual-mode closed-loop control scheme was proposed, where the driving foot trajectory is regulated via a coordinate transformation method, and a phase integration control strategy is combined with the optimization of $\eta$ to effectively suppress backward motion, thereby significantly enhancing long-range tracking accuracy. Experimental results demonstrated motion linearity with correlation coefficient of $R^{2} = 0.9999$ and bidirectional consistency of \qty{97.04}{\percent}. By optimizing the configurable coefficient, the RMS error in long-range tracking is reduced by \qty{73.7}{\percent}, achieving a theoretical resolution of \qty{0.284}{nm}, thereby ensuring high tracking performance. The actuator developed in this work extended the motion capability of piezoelectric inertial actuators by achieving cross-scale smooth tracking, besides the stepping mode of standard inertial actuators, therefore offering significant potentials in various applications such as semiconductor manufacturing and high precision measurement.

A physics-based model for individual bouncing load incorporating dynamic and kinematic characteristics of human body
abstract: In this study, a physics-based model for individual bouncing loads that integrates both the dynamic and kinematic characteristics of the human body is proposed. First, a single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) dynamic model was employed to reconstruct the ground reaction force (GRF), as GRF was found to be strongly correlated with body acceleration. Second, the kinematic relationship between the vertical displacement of the center of mass (CoM) and both geometric parameters (i.e., height) and postural configurations was established using a planetary two-segment lower limb model. Third, a comprehensive experimental campaign was conducted with 24 participants performing bouncing movements from 1.5 Hz to 3.5 Hz at 0.2 Hz intervals, while body-motion tracking and GRF were recorded simultaneously. The collected bouncing data were subsequently used to identify parameters of the physics-based model. Finally, the physics-based model was developed by integrating the dynamic and kinematic models, and was validated from both dynamic and kinematic perspectives. The proposed model shows potential advantages over traditional force models by coupling an SDOF representation of GRF with a planetary two-segment kinematic description of the lower limb. By accounting for body stiffness, damping, a frequency-dependent effective-mass participation ratio and height, it supports low-dimensional, analytical reconstruction of GRF from simple anthropometrics and posture and provides a practical interface for coupled human–structure interaction simulations; it may also facilitate non-contact, large-scale structural vibration assessment using computer vision.

title: Flexural wave trapping and vibration suppression of annular ABH metasurfaces with radial periodicity
A novel sticky Bayesian nonparametric approach for bearing damage state tracking using acoustic emission
Cross-condition tool wear prediction via feature decoupling and domain-adaptive representation learning
abstract: Tool wear prediction across varying operating conditions is challenging because wear-related degradation information is usually entangled with condition-dependent variations, which degrades prediction accuracy and cross-domain generalization. To address this issue, this paper proposes a cross-condition tool wear prediction framework based on feature decoupling and domain-adaptive representation learning. A multimodal adversarial autoencoder is first developed to learn a structured latent space, in which wear-related and condition-related information are explicitly separated. This design suppresses condition interference and yields more transferable degradation representations. A domain-adaptive prediction model with domain-aware contrastive learning is then constructed to align wear-relevant features across domains while preserving discriminative structure, thereby mitigating negative transfer caused by feature entanglement and distribution shift. Experiments on the Jilin University turning dataset and the NASA milling dataset demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms representative methods under cross-condition settings and achieves superior prediction accuracy, robustness, and generalization. The results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective solution for tool wear prediction in complex manufacturing environments.

title: DRN-PISSM: a pitch bearing fault diagnosis network integrating dilated residual convolution and a Physics-Informed State-Space model
Assessment of bridge end-support degradation from loaded frequency variation by dual-vehicle cooperative scanning: theory and experiment
Multiscale microstructures fabrication on mold steel by elliptical vibration cutting equipped with fast tool servo
Slow-sound compression and aero-acoustic performance of rainbow-trapping silencers under low-speed grazing flow
abstract: Slow-sound mechanisms are often invoked to explain broadband dissipation in rainbow-trapping silencers (RTSs), yet their robustness under grazing flow and their quantitative scaling remain largely unexplored. This study establishes a theoretical framework, assessed against numerical approaches and measurements, to elucidate slow-sound propagation and aero-acoustic performance in RTSs under low-speed grazing flow. Without flow, three wave regimes are identified – stiffness-controlled slow sound, inertial wave trapping, and fast-sound transition – governed by the effective compressibility of the resonant cavities. Closed-form asymptotic expressions derived at the quarter-wave resonance and compliance-cancellation frequencies reveal how cavity depth and visco-thermal losses enhance slow-sound or fast-sound effects across regimes. When grazing flow is introduced, near the quarter-wave resonance, interaction between convection and compressibility regularized by viscous losses reduces the expected convective shift in phase-speed, whereas near the compliance cancellation frequency, a stretching effect amplifies it. The Mach-number scaling of the slow-sound compression effect is validated on an optimized RTS prototype against the transfer matrix method, finite difference time domain model, flow-coupled finite-element method and wind-tunnel measurements up to Mach 0.09 under upstream (UPC) and downstream (DPC) propagation conditions. UPC broaden the high-dissipation plateau toward lower frequencies and DPC shift it upward. A key outcome is that the flow-induced losses further compress the UPC–DPC difference in slowed phase speeds beyond convective effects. Overall, the RTS slow-sound and dissipation performance stay robust to low-speed flow conditions. Beyond performance characterization, this work provides predictive scaling laws for the slow-sound-based optimization of compact RTSs operating under flow.

title: High-fidelity random micro-vibration reproduction via a stinger-free magneto-pneumatic platform and multi-resolution adaptive FD-ILC
abstract: High-fidelity broadband random micro-vibration reproduction is a fundamental prerequisite for vibration-isolation performance evaluation and metrological calibration of ultra-precision equipment. Unfortunately, conventional ground excitation systems generally rely on mechanical stingers for force transmission, which tend to introduce parasitic stiffness and nonlinear friction. Moreover, under random vibration conditions, standard control algorithms inherently suffer from noise amplification and steady-state overlearning, severely constraining the signal-to-noise ratio and metrological reliability of micro-vibration testing. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel non-contact, direct-drive ground excitation platform based on a stinger-free magneto-pneumatic hybrid suspension. The platform combines magnetic coupling from a voice-coil motor with air-floating guidance to establish a high-purity dynamic environment characterized by low friction and low parasitic stiffness. A multi-resolution adaptive frequency-domain iterative learning control (MRA-FD-ILC) algorithm is further developed. This algorithm integrates one-third-octave-band error evaluation with narrowband high-resolution spectral updating to effectively suppress stochastic variance disturbances and overlearning, thereby enabling stable convergence in random vibration spectral-shaping control. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system reproduces an adjustable random vibration spectrum from VC-C to VC-A over the 0.5–100 Hz frequency band. The root-mean-square spectral tracking error remains below 0.8 dB. The system also maintains stable spectral-shaping capability in the ultra-low-frequency range. The proposed method can provide important technical support for the performance evaluation of ultra-precision vibration-isolation systems.

title: End-to-end prediction and inverse identification of gear grinding and EOL performance based on physics-informed neural networks
Parallelized computation of quasi-periodic solutions for finite element problems: A Fourier series expansion-based shooting method
abstract: High-dimensional nonlinear mechanical systems admit quasi-periodic solutions that are essential for the understanding of the dynamical systems. These quasi-periodic solutions stay on some invariant tori governed by complex PDEs in hyper-time. Here, we propose a Fourier series expansion-based shooting method (FSE-Shooting) for the parallelized computation of quasi-periodic solution with $d$ base frequencies ($d \ge 2$). We represent the associated $d$-torus as a collection of trajectories initialized at a ($d-1$)-torus. We drive a set of ODEs that hold for any of these trajectories. We also derive a set of boundary conditions that couple the initial and terminal states of these trajectories and then formulate a set of nonlinear algebraic equations via the coupling conditions. We use Fourier series expansion to parameterize the ($d-1$)-torus and shooting method to iterate the Fourier coefficients associated with initial torus such that the coupling conditions are satisfied. In particular, the terminal points of these trajectories are parallelized computed via Newmark integration, where the time points and Fourier coefficients are transformed to each other by alternating Frequency-Time method. A straightforward phase condition is devised to track the quasi-periodic solutions with priori unknown base frequencies. Additionally, the by-product of the FSE-Shooting can be also directly used to compute the Lyapunov exponents to assess the stabilities of quasi-periodic solutions. The results of three finite element systems show the efficiency and versatility of FSE-Shooting in high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems, including a three-dimensional shell structure with $1872$ DOFs.

title: Fault propagation pathways and decoupling analysis of non-circulating bearing electrical erosion in integrated electric drive units

An unsupervised deep learning method for extracting weak reflections from strong guided waves in array data
abstract: The separation of overlapping wavefields in array sensor measurements is a fundamental challenge in acoustic and vibration diagnostics, with critical applications from structural health monitoring to subsurface imaging. A particularly challenging scenario occurs when extremely weak target signals (e.g., geological reflections from fractures) are completely masked by strong guided-wave interference in borehole acoustic reflection imaging. Traditional methods inadequately suppress guided waves, resulting in residual interference that obscures the weak reflections. Furthermore, supervised deep learning methods face practical constraints due to the limited availability of labeled data in field applications. To address these limitations, we propose a novel unsupervised approach that integrates the time-frequency network (TF-GridNet) with a Multi-Frame Wiener Filter (MFWF). Our approach exploits the distinct kinematic properties of guided waves and reflections in array data to achieve separation without requiring labeled training sets. Comprehensive validation on both simulated and field data from complex geological lithologies demonstrates our method’s superiority. On simulated data, it achieves a lower separation residual (L2-norm) than conventional F-K and Multichannel Singular-Spectrum Analysis (MSSA) methods. Crucially, on field data, it enables the reliable extraction of weak reflections, producing significantly clearer images of high-dip-angle fractures and fracture networks with enhanced continuity and reduced artifacts. This work presents a robust, label-free solution for extracting weak signals from strong interference in waveguide structures, as demonstrated in borehole acoustics. The method shows strong potential for advancing structural health monitoring applications that rely on guided-wave sensing.

Modeling of unbalanced magnetic pull and nonlinear dynamic analysis of rotor systems for radial permanent magnet eddy current couplers under dynamic eccentricity
abstract: Permanent magnet eddy current couplers (PMECCs), which enable non-contact torque transmission and speed regulation, are widely used in industrial equipment. Most existing research on PMECC has focused on torque transmission, while studies on radial vibration remain limited. This is because, under dynamic eccentricity, unbalanced magnetic pull (UMP) is intricately coupled with rotor motion and varies over time during rotation, significantly increasing the complexity of modeling. In this paper, an analytical model for the UMP of radial PMECCs under dynamic eccentricity is developed by combining the magnetic equivalent circuit method with the Maxwell stress tensor method, and validated by finite element analysis. A dynamic model of the rotor system is further established by incorporating multiple excitation sources, including mass imbalance, nonlinear bearing forces, gravity, and UMP. Through numerical integration of the established model, the radial vibration characteristics of the radial PMECC rotor system were quantitatively investigated in this paper. A comparison with the mechanical coupling (MC) rotor system indicates that the radial PMECC exhibits superior radial vibration reduction performance and more effectively suppresses vibrations induced by parallel misalignment. This advantage becomes increasingly significant as the staic eccentricity (ec) increases. Comparative experiments performed on a test rig validated the proposed UMP and rotor dynamic models. The results further demonstrated that the radial PMECC provides superior vibration reduction performance relative to the MC under parallel misalignment conditions. The findings provide theoretical and experimental support for analyzing the dynamic characteristics of radial PMECCs in complex rotor systems and offer guidance for engineering applications.

title: The combined use of the Hilbert–Huang Transform and the Multiple Scale Method for the parameter identification of nonlinear dynamical systems
abstract: A technique for identifying the parameters of nonlinear mechanical systems is proposed here. Time series of the system response are generated either by non-trivial initial conditions or by the action of harmonic force in conditions of external resonance. The proposed procedure combines the use of the Hilbert Huang Transform (HHT) with the Multiple Scale Method (MSM). In particular, the acquired system response is processed by the HHT, and the output is used to identify the parameters by means of a pseudo-inversion of the Amplitude Modulation Equations provided by the MSM. The procedure is applied to discrete nonlinear systems with one or two degrees of freedom, and then extended to a continuous system, consisting of a beam with geometric and material nonlinearities. Finally, as validation of the procedure, first a real-time simulation on a 1 degree of freedom nonlinear oscillator is performed, and then an experimental application on a clamped–clamped beam is carried out.

MSEEN-LightGBM via IDTCWPT for noise-robust fault diagnosis of industrial equipment
abstract: Fault evolution in industrial equipment is reflected in vibration signals through complex nonlinear and chaotic dynamics. However, traditional diagnosis methods are inherently limited in capturing such complexity and are highly sensitive to noise interference. To address these issues, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method MSEEN-LightGBM that integrates Multiscale Sparse Energy Entropy (MSEEN), and LightGBM with an enhanced loss function. First, an Improved Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Packet Transform (IDTCWPT) is proposed to address frequency aliasing and translation sensitivity. Then, a Multiscale Sparse Energy Entropy (MSEEN) is developed by integrating IDTCWPT with non-convex sparse regularization to capture multiscale fault characteristics and enable adaptive sparse feature selection. In addition, sparse energy features and multi-domain statistical features are fused and then classified using LightGBM with an enhanced loss function. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, a multi-equipment case study was conducted. The proposed method achieved 97.42% accuracy and 97.38% F1 score, with a false positive rate of 0.4% and F1 exceeding 97% across all four equipment types, while maintaining robust performance under strong noise. These results demonstrate its advantages in diagnostic accuracy, noise robustness, and generalization capability.

title: Acoustic dynamic modal analysis through Bayesian inference with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo method
Drift-controlled IMU-only displacement estimation for flexible structures using EKF and UKF
Full-field full-stress-tensor identification of base-excited structures
abstract: Identifying the full-stress tensor over the surface of a vibrating structure is essential for design validation and vibration-fatigue-life estimation, yet current experimental methods provide only pointwise or incomplete stress data. Infrared cameras can provide non-contact, full-field surface-stress measurements on vibrating structures via the thermoelastic effect; however, they measure only the first stress invariant ( i.e. , the sum of the normal stresses at the free surface: σ x x + σ y y ). The individual stress components ( σ x x , σ y y , τ x y ) required for a complete characterisation of the surface-stress state remain inaccessible from a single thermoelastic measurement. This article introduces a method that recovers the full-field, in-plane-stress power spectral density (PSD) field from thermoelastic camera data on a base-excited structure, demonstrated for thin, isotropic, metallic, plate-like structures under adiabatic conditions. First, a characterisation measurement identifies the hybrid stress-mode shapes containing all the plane-stress components by merging thermoelastic camera data with a simplified FE model through SEMM. Then, during operation under broadband random base excitation, the camera response is projected onto these mode shapes and expanded to the full-stress-tensor PSD. The method is validated experimentally on a clamped aluminium plate, identifying spatially resolved stress PSDs for all three in-plane components ( σ x x , σ y y , τ x y ). The full-field first invariant σ x x + σ y y is measured experimentally; the individual components σ x x , σ y y and τ x y are reconstructed through an experimentally corrected modal expansion informed by an FE stress basis, which supplies the inter-component ratios.

The shock isolation performance of high-performance wire rope isolators in floating raft isolation systems

A Frequency-Aware Residual Decomposition Network for Extracting Incipient Fault Signatures in Rotating Machinery
abstract: Signal decomposition is an important task in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) of mechanical transmission systems characterized by nonlinear and non-stationary vibration responses. However, conventional signal processing methodologies are often constrained by fixed basis functions and manual parameter tuning, which compromise noise robustness and limit their ability in capturing transient signatures of incipient faults. Leveraging the paradigm of signal processing-informed neural networks, this paper proposes an interpretable Frequency-Aware Residual Decomposition Network (FARCD-Net), which unfolds iterative filtering into a learnable framework to reduce reliance on manually designed optimization objectives. Specifically, a Generalized Adaptive Decomposition Module (GADM) is constructed via residual learning to generalize the conventional filtering operator, preserving the underlying decomposition principle. To enhance feature extraction in noisy environments, a data-driven Frequency Masking Layer (FML) is introduced. The layer learns adaptive spectral weights, enabling the network to dynamically localize transient signatures within resonance bands. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations on a run-to-failure benchmark and a high-speed train bogie system demonstrate effective extraction of fault-induced transients, with physical interpretability supported by intermediate network representations.

title: High-fidelity wear simulation of gas foil bearing-rotor systems in hydrogen fuel cell air compressors using a physics-guided neural network
abstract: A Gas Foil Bearing (GFB)-rotor system is critical to a hydrogen fuel cell air compressor, yet highly susceptible to wear under frequent start-stop operations. Existing simulation models rarely consider wear and lack simulation accuracy, inadequately assessing lubrication performance and frictional power loss of GFB-rotor systems. To address this issue, this study proposes a high-fidelity dynamic model for a GFB-rotor system based on a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN), coupling a physics-based GFB-rotor dynamic model with a neural network used for model error compensation. The GFB-rotor dynamic model incorporates wear-induced gas film thickness variation, Reynolds equation, foil structural dynamics, and rigid rotor motion equations. To compensate for deviations from theoretical simplifications, the neural network embeds a learnable model discrepancy term into the GFB-rotor dynamic model. The model parameters and neural network weights are then iteratively optimized via experimental calibration. The simulated results of the proposed high-fidelity model match well with experimental data, with relative errors below 5.73% across all operating conditions. Parametric analyses demonstrate that wear significantly deteriorates gas film lubrication performance. Increased wear depth and worn region reduce minimum gas film thickness, raise maximum gas film pressure, and shift the pressure field from single-peak to dual-peak concentration. Wear amplifies viscous shear dissipation via reduced gas film thickness and elevated gas film pressure, increasing frictional power loss of the GFB-rotor system by up to 44.5% under 20,000 rpm. The proposed high-fidelity model enables accurate condition monitoring of GFB-rotor systems, ensuring stable performance and optimal efficiency of hydrogen fuel cell air compressors.

SFDM: Structural full-field dynamic displacement monitoring utilizing computer vision-enhanced targetless monitoring system
abstract: Full-field dynamic displacement monitoring with high spatial resolution provides a more comprehensive representation of the dynamic characteristics of bridge structures, thereby significantly enhancing the effectiveness of bridge structural health monitoring (BSHM). In this study, a structural full-field dynamic displacement monitoring (SFDM) method is proposed to overcome the limitations of traditional discrete-point measurement techniques. To achieve targetless and accurate extraction of the lower edge of bridge structures, an effective computer vision framework is developed by integrating a robust fusion image processing (RFIP) strategy with a row-wise adaptive edge detection (RAED) approach. Additionally, a multi-target displacement transformation model (MDTM) is proposed to convert subpixel-level image displacements into physical displacements. A tied-arch bridge field test was conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The experimental results indicate that the proposed SFDM achieved correlation coefficients higher than 0.964, while the corresponding RMSE and NRMSE remained below 0.282 mm and 9.178% across all test cases, respectively, thereby confirming its accuracy and effectiveness for full-field displacement monitoring in BSHM applications.

Free interface blade mistuning model: Experimental validation with measured blade variability and contact conditions
abstract: Accurate modeling of mistuning in bladed disks requires a consistent representation of blade-to-blade variability and its impact on the assembled system dynamics. This work presents an experimental validation of a reduced-order modeling approach for mistuned bladed disks, where the variability of individual components is directly derived from measurements. Free–free modal hammer tests are performed on individual blades to quantify the dispersion in natural frequencies arising from manufacturing tolerances and geometric variability. These experimentally measured perturbations are introduced into the reduced-order formulation of the blade component, enabling a physically consistent representation of intrinsic mistuning. The finite element model of the disk is updated based on experimental data, and the full assembly is modeled using a component mode synthesis framework, combining Rubin reduction for the blades and Craig–Bampton reduction for the disk. The assembled bladed disk is experimentally characterized through modal testing, and the numerical predictions are compared against the measured natural frequencies and mode shapes. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach accurately captures the effect of blade variability on the global dynamic behavior. The study highlights the effectiveness of incorporating experimentally derived blade properties into reduced-order model, providing a robust and physically interpretable framework for the analysis of mistuned bladed disks.

Dimension-reduced probability density evolution equation for spatial three-dimensional vehicle-rail-bridge partitioned system
abstract: Stochastic dynamic response analysis of three-dimensional (3D) vehicle-rail-bridge (VRB) systems is challenging due to time-varying coupling, high-dimensional uncertainties, and strongly nonstationary and non-Gaussian response characteristics. This study develops an efficient stochastic dynamic analysis framework by introducing the dimension-reduced probability density evolution equation (DR-PDEE) into a non-iterative partitioned VRB model. The vehicle, rail, and bridge subsystems are formulated as time-invariant stochastic subsystems connected through time-dependent wheel-rail and time-independent rail-bridge interfaces, thereby avoiding repeated assembly and factorization of global time-varying system matrices. Based on this deterministic backbone, the DR-PDEE is used to characterize the time-varying probability density evolution of selected displacement responses under random system parameters and stochastic track irregularities. To improve numerical robustness for highly nonstationary and non-Gaussian VRB responses, a dimension-reduced Monte Carlo solution strategy is adopted for solving the DR-PDEE and compared with the classical path-integration scheme. Numerical results are validated against Monte Carlo simulations with 10,000 realizations. The proposed framework accurately captures nonstationary and non-Gaussian response distributions using a limited number of samples, demonstrating its efficiency and potential for stochastic analysis of complex coupled railway systems.

Magnetic-gear-enabled counter-rotating electromagnetic energy harvester for capturing low-speed wind energy
abstract: Wind energy is an abundant ambient power source for self-powered sensing, but conventional electromagnetic wind harvesters remain constrained under weak wind due to low rotor speed and limited magnetic flux variation. To address this issue, this paper presents a magnetic-gear-enabled Savonius-driven counter-rotating electromagnetic energy harvester (MG-SCR-EMEH) that integrates a Savonius turbine, an axial magnetic gear, and upper and lower electromagnetic power-generation modules. A non-contact magnetic speed amplification mechanism and a coaxial counter-rotating configuration triple the effective magnet-coil relative speed over direct-drive, thereby enhancing the magnetic flux variation and induction output while avoiding the wear and dissipation of contact-based frequency up-conversion. A theoretical model that combines aerodynamic drag and induced-voltage analyses, supported by finite element simulations, elucidates the mechanisms of magnetic-field modulation, torque transmission, and voltage generation. Experimental results show that the proposed MG-SCR-EMEH starts up at 3.5 m/s and, at 4.5 m/s, delivers 5.552 mW system-level equivalent charging power (27.76 mJ over 5 s into a 1 mF capacitor, 1.903 W/m 3 power density). At the same input speed of 50 RPM, increasing the magnet-coil relative speed from 50 RPM in the direct-drive configuration to 150 RPM in the magnetic-gear-coupled configuration raises the peak power from 22.78 to 166.78 mW. Furthermore, integrated with an energy-management unit, layered millimeter-wave radar nodes, and a BLE module, the MG-SCR-EMEH serves as the power source for a falling-object warning system, highlighting strong potential for low-speed wind energy harvesting and structural safety monitoring.

Q-shift dual-tree complex wavelet phase-based vibration displacement measurement for wind turbine towers
abstract: In the context of the global energy transition, wind turbine towers serve as the primary load-bearing structures of wind energy systems, and accurate measurement of their vibration-induced displacements is essential for structural health monitoring and safety assessment. Conventional contact-based measurement techniques suffer from complex installation procedures and limited spatial coverage. In contrast, existing vision-based vibration measurement methods are often highly dependent on surface texture and exhibit insufficient phase stability under challenging imaging conditions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a non-contact vibration displacement measurement method for wind turbine towers based on the phase information of the Q-shift dual-tree complex wavelet transform. The proposed approach exploits the multi-scale and multi-directional complex coefficients obtained from the Q-shift dual-tree complex wavelet decomposition to construct a phase representation with approximate shift invariance and improved inter-scale consistency. Displacement estimation is performed within regions exhibiting stable phase responses, such as structural edges, thereby enhancing robustness against complex backgrounds and noise. Furthermore, an adaptive downsampling strategy is introduced to alleviate phase wrapping effects in large-scale structural vibrations, enabling reliable displacement measurement under relatively large vibration amplitudes. Numerical simulations and wind turbine tower model experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves sub-pixel displacement accuracy under complex environmental conditions. Compared with conventional vision-based approaches based on phase or image intensity information, the proposed method exhibits superior overall stability, providing a high-precision and robust visual vibration measurement solution for the non-contact monitoring of tall and flexible structures.

title: Bayesian learning in structural dynamics: a comprehensive review and emerging trends
abstract: Bayesian learning has emerged as a compelling and vital research direction in the field of structural dynamics, offering a probabilistic lens to understand and refine the analysis of complex dynamical systems. This review meticulously traces the three-decade evolution of Bayesian learning in structural dynamics, illuminating core principles, groundbreaking methodologies, and diverse applications that have significantly influenced the field. The narrative commences by delving into the basics of Bayesian theory, clarifying essential concepts, and introducing primary methods for deriving posterior distributions, with an in-depth exploration of three types: Laplace approximation, stochastic sampling, and variational inference. Subsequently, the text explores the implementation of two types of Bayesian learning in structural dynamics: physical model learning and data-centric statistical model learning. Physical model learning emphasizes inferring physical model parameters within a Bayesian framework for system identification and prediction, while statistical model learning integrates Bayesian learning methodologies into data-centric statistical modeling within probabilistic machine learning. Both types resonate across various applications, such as modal analysis, model updating, damage detection, and reliability updating, highlighting their pivotal role in enhancing comprehension of dynamical systems and decision-making. The paper also navigates obstacles by proposing ways to enhance existing Bayesian inference strategies. Distinguished from previous research, this study offers a thorough examination of both traditional and cutting-edge Bayesian methods. It not only underscores the transformative influence of Bayesian approaches but also serves as a beacon, guiding researchers in the judicious selection and refinement of suitable methods for various challenges in structural dynamics.

Novel non-contact adjustable torsional electromagnetic negative stiffness device: Theoretical analysis and application
abstract: To address the issue that traditional quasi-zero-stiffness (QZS) torsional vibration isolation systems struggle to adapt to time-varying loads due to their fixed structural parameters, this paper proposes a novel non-contact adjustable torsional electromagnetic negative stiffness device (ATENSD). Through the axial electromagnetic coupling between the iron-core coils and the permanent magnets, the ATENSD can generate rotational negative stiffness which can be dynamically adjusted by regulating the current of the iron-core coil. Firstly, the fundamental configuration of the ATENSD is introduced, and the principle of its variable negative stiffness is analyzed. Subsequently, electromagnetic finite element analysis are employed to elucidate the influence of the permanent magnet shape, the permanent magnet thickness, the pole-pair number and the magnetic-pole angle on the ATENSD stiffness characteristics, for guiding the prototype design. Moreover, the analytical electromagnetic-force model of the ATENSD is established by the magnetic energy method. And a comparative analysis is then conducted to examine the influence laws of the control current and the air gap on the electromagnetic torque and stiffness characteristics of the ATENSD. Finally, stiffness characterization experiments and vibration transmission test experiments are conducted on the ATENSD prototype. The results demonstrate that the designed ATENSD achieves continuously adjustable negative stiffness with good linearity during current regulation. And the QZS adjustable electromagnetic torsional isolator (QZS-AETI), integrated with the ATENSD, has a good vibration transmission suppression effect across the entire frequency range.

title: Restoring force modeling of preloaded metal rubber pairs (PMRP) considering component asymmetry for nonlinear vibration analysis
An enhanced method for instantaneous angular speed accuracy improvement and its application in variable-speed scenarios
abstract: Tacholess speed estimation serves as a powerful preprocessing method for condition monitoring of variable-speed machinery in scenarios where speed reference sensors are unavailable. However, for a mono amplitude modulated (AM)-frequency modulated (FM) signal contaminated by background noise, the instantaneous frequency (IF) retrieved via phase demodulation tends to fluctuate around its theoretical value. In this study, we first derive the influence of three key factors—carrier signal amplitude, amplitude modulation characteristics, and background noise variance—on the fluctuation (i.e., variance) of the estimated IF. Based on this theoretical insight, instantaneous angular speed (IAS) estimates derived from all vibration harmonics, together with their corresponding instantaneous IAS variance, can be estimated from the vibration signal. The optimal IAS estimate is then obtained by leveraging the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) framework. Accordingly, this study proposes an enhanced IAS accuracy improvement (EIASAI) method for iterative refinement of IAS estimation accuracy. The efficacy of the proposed method is evaluated and benchmarked against existing state-of-the-art methods using both numerical simulations and vibration signals collected from operational wind turbines.

title: Resonance response identification and vibration damping analysis of thin-walled spiral bevel gear
A Physics-Guided adversarial compensation framework for the dynamic viscoelastic errors in flexible pressure sensors
Autocorrelation weighted enhanced envelope spectrum for compound bearing fault diagnosis
A novel low-intervention blade tip micro-Doppler vibration measurement method to avoid undersampling

Analysis of local fault coupling mechanism and dynamic response characteristics in dual-rotor system
Design and vibration reduction characteristics of a hollow multi-chambered particle-damped milling cutter inspired by the lotus root structure
abstract: Chatter vibration in milling adversely affects machining stability, surface integrity, and tool life, especially in lightweight or slender tool systems. To enhance vibration suppression while retaining structural lightweight potential, this study proposes a lotus-root-inspired multi-chambered particle-damped milling cutter (LRMC), in which a biomimetic hollow multi-cavity architecture is integrated with distributed particle damping. An energy analysis model was developed by considering structural damping, particle-particle and particle-wall collision dissipation, and interparticle friction dissipation. Geometric morphology margin and constrained-scale margin were introduced to describe the effects of cavity shape, particle diameter, filling ratio, and particle mobility on energy dissipation. Static impact tests and dynamic milling experiments were conducted to evaluate LRMCs with different particle filling ratios. The results show that particle filling significantly improves the dynamic behavior of the hollow multi-chambered cutter by suppressing modal compliance and broadband vibration response. Among the tested configurations, the 36.8%-filled LRMC exhibits the best overall vibration reduction performance, reducing the primary modal peak compliance by 80.5% compared with the empty LRMC and reducing high-frequency acceleration RMS by 50.2%-64.5% compared with the solid toolholder during milling. Acoustic emission analysis further confirms improved cutting stability, with RMS reductions of 27.6%-43.6% relative to the solid toolholder. These findings demonstrate that the lotus-root-inspired particle-damped structure provides an effective strategy for developing lightweight milling cutters with enhanced vibration suppression and machining stability.

title: Fusing multi-sensor data in graph convolutional networks for robust structural damage detection against environmental and operational variations
Mechanism of dynamic response amplification of ropeway cables: Numerical and experimental investigation
abstract: Cables are used in many engineering applications, including transport systems in which mobile cables suspended between supports are used to move attached vehicles. Such systems are prone to self-sustained, high-amplitude oscillations owing to their intrinsic nonlinear nature and the evolution of their dynamic characteristics during steady-state operation. A framework is therefore needed to understand the influence of design parameters on dynamic behaviour and to predict oscillation amplitudes. This paper presents a mechanical model of ropeway cable dynamics, enabling extraction of the modal content and incorporation of nonlinearities. An experimental investigation is then carried out on a real chairlift case study through field measurements, combining video analysis and on-site sensor data, to characterise the dynamic amplification phenomena and the hierarchy of mechanical couplings between the vehicles, the drive system, and the cable. Finally, a transient simulation is performed based on modal decomposition and a reduced-order dynamic model, incorporating parametric excitation induced by cable tension variations, geometric nonlinearities, and nonlinear coupling between the pumping mode and the out-of-plane mode. A test/simulation comparison is conducted for model updating and calibration. The main contributions of this study are: (i) an analysis of the coupled mechanisms underlying the onset of cable pumping based on field measurements; (ii) a coupled multi-span dynamic modelling framework for ropeway cable loops capturing vertical-longitudinal modal interactions under operational conditions; (iii) a reduced-order model built from a pumping-mode subspace enabling nonlinear transient simulations; (iv) surrogate parameters accounting for unmodelled coupling effects such as cable torsion, vehicle swaying, and bullwheel drive dynamics; and (v) experimental calibration and model updating based on in-situ measurements of cable pumping.

title: Investigation into the dynamic behaviour of rotors supported on starved bearings
abstract: This paper presents an experimental and numerical investigation of rotor vibration when a cylindrical journal bearing experiences oil starvation. The primary goals are to enhance the current available experimental data and provide a detailed comparison between starvation models based on experimentally measured rotor vibration responses. A dedicated test rig equipped with two active magnetic bearings was used to levitate and accurately position the rotor shaft at controlled eccentricities, allowing stable and repeatable testing across a broad range of operating conditions. A single hydrodynamic bearing was mounted on the rig, and lubricant flow was progressively reduced to induce starvation. Shaft displacements were measured and thoroughly characterized in time and frequency domains. The experimental results revealed an increase in synchronous vibration under starvation, mainly in a backward whirl component. A low-amplitude, broadband subsynchronous vibration (SSV) was also observed, which is reported as a new rotordynamic feature associated with oil film instability in cylindrical bearings. Numerical simulations were performed using a mass-conserving starvation model with two different inlet boundary conditions: prescribed inlet oil fraction and prescribed inlet flow rate. The results demonstrate that the models produce a distinctive pressure distribution, hence, a different rotor response. The inlet oil fraction boundary condition showed the best agreement with the measurements.

Two-scale concurrent structural topology optimization for transient wave energy-flow control
abstract: Structural energy-flow control enables functionalities such as vibration shielding and energy harvesting, and is of great significance in fields such as aerospace engineering, precision instrumentation, and rail transportation. However, structural design methods for achieving prescribed energy-flow control functionalities remain underexplored. This study proposes a two-scale concurrent topology optimization method for transient wave energy-flow control. To achieve different energy-flow control functionalities, three representative optimization objectives are considered: energy-flow blocking, energy-flow focusing, and zigzag energy-flow routing. The expression for transient energy-flow is derived from the differential form of energy conservation. To suppress the influence of boundary reflections, a Laplace-equation-based absorbing boundary condition is formulated. In the proposed two-scale topology optimization framework, the effective elasticity matrix of the microstructure is evaluated based on the homogenization theory. At the microscopic scale, inter-microstructure connectivity constraints, together with virtual-temperature-based connectivity constraints, are introduced for single-material topology optimization, thereby ensuring the manufacturability of the optimized designs. To obtain diverse optimized configurations, the initial designs are generated using random morphology description functions (RMDFs). In the numerical examples, both bi-material and single-material optimization results are presented for the three optimization objectives. The results show that energy-flow tends to propagate along the direction of maximum stiffness, while the impedance mismatch between different microstructures also affects its propagation direction. These findings suggest that the proposed method has potential applications in structural vibration control, energy dissipation, and energy harvesting.

title: From sparse measurements to probabilistic solution manifolds: an FCWV inverse framework for parameter identification and full-field reconstruction
abstract: Strongly nonlinear and underdetermined inverse problems commonly arise in structural health monitoring, model updating, and deformation reconstruction, where sparse measurements may correspond to multiple admissible parameter combinations. This work presents a probabilistic finite cell weight variation (FCWV)-based inverse framework capable of reconstructing full admissible solution manifolds together with their associated probability distributions. The formulation is derived from the conservation law of probability and the transformation law of probability density, and recursively decomposes a multi-dimensional inverse problem into coupled one-dimensional searches. In this way, admissible solution manifolds can be identified efficiently without reliance on large-scale global optimization or extensive Bayesian sampling. The framework is developed for multi-input, multi-output systems and extended to higher-dimensional inverse problems through a recursive sampling strategy. Two benchmark examples are considered. The first involves identification of unknown parameters in a nonlinear analytical leak-rate model for a cracked pipe using prescribed leak-rate measurements, where the inverse formulation is validated against direct uncertainty propagation. The second considers a beam-element piping system under seismic excitation, in which six unknown support stiffnesses are identified from prescribed target displacement responses at a node, using a surrogate response model constructed from finite element simulations. In both examples, the proposed method successfully reconstructs admissible solution manifolds and quantifies the relative likelihood of competing solutions. The results demonstrate that the FCWV-based inverse framework provides an efficient and physically transparent alternative for solving strongly nonlinear and underdetermined inverse problems with sparse measurements.

title: Parameter identification and unknown excitation inversion of piezoelectric cantilever beams using multi-network PINNs with Fourier feature mapping

Integrated physics-informed and unsupervised learning assessment of hemp-reinforced masonry barrel vaults under shaking table testing
abstract: The seismic assessment of strengthened masonry vaults through full-scale shaking-table testing remains limited, particularly for sustainable, heritage-compatible systems. This study investigates the dynamic response and damage evolution of full-scale masonry barrel vaults strengthened with a hemp-mesh biocomposite embedded in a cocciopesto matrix. A two-phase experimental campaign was carried out on two geometrically identical vaults subjected to progressively scaled three-component earthquake records, enabling the analysis of three representative structural configurations: unreinforced, newly reinforced, and damaged-then-reinforced. Reinforcement effectiveness and damage progression were assessed through a multi-indicator framework combining modal parameters with two proposed indicators: an energy-based indicator derived from Arias intensity and an autoencoder-based indicator. Each is formulated in a baseline-relative (excitation-dependent) form and in an input-normalized form where the energy-based indicator is normalized by the Arias intensity of the input and the autoencoder-based indicator by the squared RMS of the input. It follows that the input-normalized indicators isolate structural regime transitions from the excitation amplitude growth. Results show that the reinforcement, in both newly reinforced and damaged-then-reinforced configurations, enhances seismic capacity and damage tolerance, with delayed damage onset and reduced stiffness degradation. The proposed indicators consistently captured structural regime transitions and damage evolution across all configurations, showing strong agreement with modal trends. In particular, energy-based indicators provide a straightforward signal-level description of regime changes, while the feature-based autoencoder approach proves effective in detecting subtle statistical deviations that may precede visible damage, confirming its effectiveness in tracking stiffness degradation and nonlinear structural response.

title: Latent dynamics-based reconstruction of large gaps in vehicle responses of stationary vehicle-bridge systems

Nonlinear dynamic modeling and experimental validation of rotor drop onto auxiliary bearings in a horizontal AMB system
abstract: Active Magnetic Bearings (AMB) are widely utilized in high-speed rotating machinery due to their frictionless operation, low energy consumption, and controllable stiffness and damping. However, the rotor drops onto auxiliary bearings (AB) caused by AMB overload or failure triggers intense nonlinear impacts and frictional heat accumulation, posing a severe threat to system safety. Current simulations of this process face significant challenges, particularly regarding the numerical stability and accuracy of the dynamic response under nonlinear transient impact conditions. To address these issues, this paper establishes a nonlinear dynamic model of a horizontal AMB-supported rigid rotor-AB system. The elastic hysteresis torque between the rotor and the AB inner race is introduced innovatively, which effectively suppresses the non-physical divergent backward whirl commonly encountered in high-speed simulations, thereby enhancing computational stability. Furthermore, a nonlinear equivalent viscous damping theory is employed to characterize the normal contact force, which is consistent with the physical reality that normal energy is not conserved during the drop impact. A high-stiffness and high-damping linear spring model is proposed for efficient tangential contact force calculation, simplifying the originally complex state-switching logic while balancing computational efficiency and precision. This study provides an effective analytical tool for understanding the dynamic impact behavior of rotor drop, offering significant theoretical value and engineering implications for the design and reliability assessment of AMB protection systems.

Physics-informed unit-normalized selective embedding with harmonic loss for fault identification using vibration and acoustic signals
abstract: Induction motors generate vibration and acoustic signals from mechanical imbalance, electromagnetic forces, and structural transmission through the machine housing. Interpreting harmonic fault signatures from these responses becomes difficult when different types of sensors are used due to bandwidth and signal scaling limitations. This work investigates how physics-informed signal representation can improve fault diagnosis using both industrial sensors and cell phone sensors. A unit-consistent normalization approach is introduced to allow comparison between vibration acceleration and acoustic pressure signals by converting both signals into equivalent vibration velocity representations. Based on this formulation, a structured signal processing framework named Unit-Normalized Selective Embedding with Harmonic Loss (UNSE-HL) is proposed, combining unit normalization, selective embedding, and a physics-informed harmonic loss function to improve the representation of modulation patterns during diagnosis. Experiments are conducted using the induction motor datasets collected under multiple operating conditions with both structurally mounted sensors and cell phones. Envelope spectral analysis shows that rotor harmonics are observable across cell phone sensors after normalization; this observability does not by itself establish classification reliability, which is evaluated separately. Time-frequency representations combined with the proposed embedding strategy improve diagnosis accuracy and classification stability relative to conventional signal representation approaches on the datasets and devices evaluated in this study. These findings highlight the importance of signal transmission physics in condition monitoring and indicate that, for the specific smartphone sensors and operating conditions tested here, appropriate preprocessing improves the usability of low-bandwidth sensors for fault diagnosis.

title: Image-to-image translation-based visual vibration displacement measurement of a rotating body with tilted viewing angle in horizontal plane
A fully multivariate multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis method for fault diagnosis
abstract: We propose a fully multivariate generalization of multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MFDFA) and leverage it to develop a fault diagnosis framework for multichannel machine vibration data. We introduce a novel covariance-weighted $L_{pq}$ matrix norm based on Mahalanobis distance to define a fully multivariate fluctuation function that uniquely captures cross-channel dependencies and variance biases in multichannel vibration data. This formulation, termed FM-MFDFA, allows for a more accurate characterization of the multiscale structure of multivariate signals. To enhance feature relevance, the proposed framework integrates multivariate variational mode decomposition (MVMD) to isolate fault-relevant components before applying FM-MFDFA. Results on wind turbine gearbox data demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional MFDFA approaches by effectively distinguishing between healthy and faulty machine states, even under noisy conditions.

Correlation analysis between dynamic cutting characteristics and workpiece surface integrity in whirling milling
abstract: Among the physical parameters that govern surface integrity, cutting vibration and cutting force play an especially crucial role. Most studies have focused on the influence of single time-series cutting force signals or cutting vibration signals on surface integrity, with limited research addressing the coupling of triaxial cutting forces or triaxial vibrations. Consequently, the critical modal information arising from the synergistic motion of the three axes has been overlooked, making it difficult to elucidate the comprehensive influence of dynamic cutting characteristics on surface integrity. This study investigates the intrinsic relationship between dynamic cutting characteristics and workpiece surface integrity by employing JRP and JRQA based on triaxial cutting force and vibration signals acquired during the whirling milling process. The raw dynamic cutting characteristic signals were denoised using a Butterworth filter and subsequently standardized to eliminate dimensional effects. Based on this, joint recurrence plots were constructed and key joint recurrence parameters (JDET, JLAM, JRPDE) were extracted. The dynamic cutting characteristics were then systematically quantified using the JRQA method. Finally, the correlation between the JRQA parameters and surface integrity data was revealed by integrating both sets of results. The research indicates that the influence of JRQA parameters on surface integrity exhibits significant conditional dependence and selectivity, with correlations varying markedly with changes in cutting parameters. In most cases, JDET and JLAM exhibit a significant negative correlation with surface roughness, particularly showing strong associations when cutting speed increases (correlation coefficient reaching -0.80). Whereas when depth of cut increases, both parameters demonstrate a strong positive correlation with residual stress (correlation coefficient reaching 0.80). JRPDE shows a perfect negative correlation with surface roughness as the number of tools increases (correlation coefficient -1.00), demonstrating strong potential for prediction and control. Furthermore, the study reveals that the contribution of JRQA factors to surface roughness and residual stress is often inconsistent, indicating that multi-objective trade-offs need to be considered when applying recurrence parameters in process optimization.

Continuum and lumped-parameter modeling of a dielectric elastomer array actuator system
abstract: This paper presents the modeling of a soft array of interconnected dielectric elastomer actuators (DEAs). The array exploits selective actuation of dielectric patches through the application of a high voltage to achieve localized deformations. The soft nature of the system induces electro-mechanical coupling between neighboring DEAs, whose interplay with the elastomer’s large deformations and viscoelasticity results in a highly complex and nonlinear dynamic response. Motivated by the need to model those effects in an accurate and computationally-efficient way, so as to enable both design optimization and real-time control, we present a set of models with different levels of complexity and accuracy. First, we introduce a continuum model formulation able to predict the dynamic electro-mechanical response of the overall array, including coupling effects and local deformation patterns, in a completely physics-based fashion. Second, we develop a control-oriented dynamic model that predicts the average response with a significantly reduced number of variables (and, in turn, lower computation burden), while still accounting for several key physical mechanisms of the underlying system. While the former accurately infers the coupled system response solely from material and geometry data, the latter requires a dedicated parameter identification procedure that is here cast as a numerically-efficient optimization problem. Both approaches are extensively validated on an experimental DEA array prototype, demonstrating high accuracy under both static and dynamic actuation.

title: Time–frequency representation of nonlinear structural response through rationally sampled Stockwell analysis
abstract: The reliable analysis of the non-stationary response of mechanical and structural systems under transient excitations, and in particular the tracking of the time-varying evolution of the dominant modal frequencies during damaging events, remains a long-standing challenge for vibration-based monitoring. A persistent practical limitation is that the time-frequency map on which any subsequent automatic or learning-based identification stage relies is built on a frequency grid that depends on implementation choices. This means that records acquired on different sensors or under different events cannot be compared on a common substrate.The present article addresses the limitation at the representational level by introducing the Stockwell-Ditommaso-Ponzo representation (SDP), obtained by sampling the Stockwell transform on an ordered Farey grid of primitive rational frequencies. Each coefficient is assigned a rational label, an ordered Voronoi frequency cell and an exact logarithmic quadrature weight induced by the Stockwell measure. Subsequent to the declaration of the sampling frequency, the analysed band and the maximum conductor, the support, the cells and the weights are uniquely determined prior to the processing of any record. A time-varying modal frequency, such as that observed when the apparent lateral stiffness of an instrumented building degrades under strong-motion excitation and partially recovers afterwards, is therefore encoded as a deterministic path on a geometry shared across sensors, repeated events and simulations of the same structure.The representation is exercised on the simulated top-floor acceleration of a five-storey reinforced-concrete infilled frame, whose apparent first-mode frequency is observed to drop to approximately 0.8 Hz and partially recovers through the simulated closure of column cracks under gravity. The SDP cell-path captures the four phases of the loss-and-recovery sequence, and engineering-oriented descriptors take values consistent with the physical setup. The proposed representation is intended to function as a reproducible, transform-level front end on which calibrated automatic identification and damage-assessment procedures, including artificial-intelligence-based pipelines, can be built in a controlled manner.

title: Bandgap theoretical prediction and broadband vibration reduction of plate-type elastic metastructure with nonlinear particle damping
Interpretable U-Net RCNN for blind peak detection in vibration spectra
abstract: Accurate peak detection in vibration spectra is key to early fault diagnosis but remains challenging due to noise and unknown spectral content. This paper presents a hybrid approach combining the benefits of U-Nets and Region-based Convolutional Neural Networks for blind peak detection, trained on complex simulated 1D data with extension to real-world signals. The model combines classification and regression to identify and localise peaks without prior knowledge of the signal or machine. Its performance is benchmarked against the Exact Order Model Estimation of Signal Parameters via Rotational Invariance Technique and a Topological Peak Identification approach using labelled simulated data, demonstrating robustness and practical effectiveness. The method is further tested on real offshore wind turbine data, where it successfully detects visually identifiable peaks, confirming its applicability in real-world scenarios.

title: Intelligent non-destructive evaluation of complex defects using magnetization-excited infrared thermography
MILT: A latent temporal framework for domain generalization in bearing fault diagnosis
Numerical and experimental analysis of a bolted-joint rotor-bearing system with squirrel cage elastic supports during speed-up process
Quickest change detection via statistical electrical signature analysis for motor diagnosis
abstract: Electrical Signature Analysis (ESA) is a widely adopted non-intrusive technique for monitoring induction motors, offering the advantage of using both current and voltage information. However, detecting early-stage faults remains a challenge due to low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and spectral pollution from the power grid that masks weak fault signatures. This paper introduces a robust statistical detection framework designed to identify incipient mechanical and electrical faults despite these constraints. First, a signal enhancement strategy combining Instantaneous Symmetrical Components (ISC) and voltage-referenced multi-variable Wiener filtering is proposed. This approach effectively suppresses grid-induced harmonics to isolate the residual fault signature within the stator current. Based on a unified physical model of torque oscillations, a local spectral health indicator is derived. Statistical analysis demonstrates that this indicator follows a Gamma distribution, the parameters of which are conditioned by the motor's operating point. To address this dependency, an operating point clustering stage, based on the active power estimated from ESA, is proposed to segment the data. Finally, a Generalized Cumulative Sum (CuSum) algorithm, explicitly derived for the Gamma distribution, is developed. Unlike memoryless static detectors such as the Neyman-Pearson test, this sequential approach exploits the temporal history of the indicator to minimize detection delay. Experimental validation on $4$kW induction motors under misalignment and broken rotor bar conditions confirms that the proposed method significantly outperforms standard detection strategies, offering high sensitivity to incipient faults even under light load conditions.

title: Deep learning based reconstruction of fiber orientation in short fiber reinforced composites from ultrasonic wave responses
abstract: Fiber orientation plays an important role in the mechanical behavior of short fiber-reinforced composites, yet its internal distribution is difficult to characterize nondestructively. This study proposes a deep learning-based framework to reconstruct fiber orientation fields from boundary ultrasonic wave responses. A two-dimensional anisotropic wave propagation model with free-boundary conditions was developed to simulate wave signals in composite plates, where the local anisotropy was governed by sectional fiber orientation. Based on this model, a synthetic dataset was generated using a sectional representation of the plate. The simulated sensor signals were used as inputs to a multilayer perceptron, while the section-wise principal-direction angles were encoded using an angle aware representation to account for periodicity. The trained model directly predicted the orientation field from the simulated boundary wave responses. Reconstruction accuracy was evaluated using wrap-aware angular error metrics. Parametric studies were conducted to examine the effects of dataset size, excitation frequency, anisotropy strength, sensor ablation, and wave transmission factor on prediction performance. The results show that the proposed framework can effectively reconstruct the main features of the section-wise principal-direction field and remains reasonably robust under varying sensing and material conditions. The proposed approach provides a promising data-driven strategy for nondestructive characterization of internal fiber orientation in short fiber-reinforced composites.
